feed.title: Garmin Forerunner 165 Music targets runners who want premium GPS without the flagship price
feed.summary: Garmin has released the Forerunner 165 Music, a new GPS running watch designed for everyday runners who desire premium features like a bright AMOLED display, reliable GPS, and on-wrist music at a more accessible price point. This model aims to bridge the gap between entry-level trackers and high-end flagship watches, offering features previously found in pricier models to a broader audience. It serves Garmin's strategy to retain its user base and appeal to serious amateur runners who are not looking for the most expensive devices.

feed.title: Qualcomm Inc Stock (QCOM) Opened Up by 3.03% on Jun 16: What Signal Does It Send?
feed.summary: Qualcomm Inc. (QCOM) stock rose 3.03% due to optimism surrounding a potential acquisition of AI chip startup Tenstorrent for $8-10 billion and increased analyst price targets ahead of its Investor Day. CEO Cristiano Amon’s vision for AI-enabled devices and a supportive macroeconomic environment further contributed to the stock's upward movement. However, the company faces risks such as acquisition integration challenges, geopolitical overhangs, potential multiple contraction, and continued margin compression in its licensing division due to Apple's transition away from Qualcomm modems.

feed.title: TSMC and Amkor sign 10-year deal to expand semiconductor packaging in Arizona
feed.summary: TSMC and Amkor Technology have entered a 10-year agreement to significantly expand advanced semiconductor packaging and test services in Peoria, Arizona, with a $7 billion facility expected to begin production by 2028. This partnership aims to create a more robust domestic chip supply chain in the US by co-locating packaging operations near TSMC's fabrication plant, leveraging technologies like InFO and CoWoS crucial for AI and high-performance computing. The initiative is strongly aligned with the CHIPS and Science Act, aiming to reduce reliance on overseas manufacturing and mitigate geopolitical risks for critical chip production.

feed.title: New BlackBerry tools let governments manage Macs without public cloud
feed.summary: BlackBerry (NYSE:BB) has announced significant enhancements to its Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) platform, addressing the growing demand for sovereign endpoint control, particularly among governments and regulated industries. The new capabilities, expected to roll out in summer 2026, include on-premises macOS management, post-quantum cryptography upgrades aligning with NIST standards for FIPS 140-3 accreditation, expanded multi-tenant support, and secure AI-assisted operations. These updates enable organizations to manage diverse device fleets without reliance on public cloud infrastructure, mitigating data residency and exfiltration risks.

feed.title: UBS AG (AMUB) sells $29.48M autocallable GEARS due June 14, 2029
feed.summary: UBS AG has issued $29.48 million in Trigger Autocallable GEARS linked to a basket of 29 equities, maturing on June 14, 2029. These securities feature an autocall barrier at 100% of the initial basket level with a 22% call return rate. If not automatically called, the maturity payoff depends on basket performance with a 1.75 upside gearing and a downside threshold of 75%, exposing investors to potential principal loss.

feed.title: Old phones, new money: $1.63B in upgrades from trade-ins
feed.summary: Assurant's Q1 2026 Mobile Trade-In and Upgrade Industry Trends Report reveals that consumers received $1.63 billion in value through mobile trade-in programs, a 31% increase from 2025. This growth is driven by rising smartphone prices, the increasing demand for refurbished devices, and the role of protection plans in maintaining device condition for higher trade-in values. The report highlights how trade-ins help offset upgrade costs, expand access to more affordable smartphones, and support a circular mobile economy.

feed.title: Italy's antitrust regulator probes Apple over cloud services under Digital Market rules
feed.summary: Italy's antitrust regulator has launched an investigation into Apple regarding its compliance with the European Digital Markets Act. The probe focuses on whether Apple ensures third-party cloud service providers can inter-operate with its iOS and iPadOS operating systems and have equal access to components as its iCloud service. This marks the first such investigation by the Italian watchdog under the DMA, with findings to be shared with the EU Commission.

feed.title: All Apple Intelligence Features Coming In iOS 27
feed.summary: Apple is set to release iOS 27 later this fall, introducing a comprehensive suite of enhanced Apple Intelligence features, many of which leverage a partnership with Google and custom Gemini models. feed.title: Apple Seeks Dismissal of Former Employee’s Discrimination/Retaliation Suit
feed.summary: Apple Inc. is seeking to dismiss a lawsuit filed by a former employee who claims he was wrongfully fired from his technical specialist position in 2022 due to his diabetes and related health issues. Apple argues that the employee, Connor Young, was justly terminated for repeatedly failing to comply with attendance policies, while Young alleges he was targeted and harassed by a supervisor because of his medical condition. The company maintains it granted all medically-supported accommodations and consistently supported him during his employment.

AAT holds US Patent No. 7,092,539 related to these microphone arrays.

feed.title: Telomir publishes preclinical data on diabetes treatment candidate By Investing.com

Despite a 36% share decline over the past year, the company, with a $43.3 million market cap, holds more cash than debt, which is crucial for clinical-stage drug developers. feed.title: Fox Corp Buying Roku In $22B Deal
feed.summary: Fox Corp has announced a $22 billion deal to acquire connected TV service Roku, significantly boosting its streaming capabilities six years after purchasing Tubi. The agreement, valued at $160 per share, will see Fox shareholders own 73% of the merged business, creating a scaled next-generation media and technology company focused on live sports, news, and the continued rise of streaming. Both companies expect the deal to be accretive to free cash flow by the second full year after closing and achieve $400 million in cost synergies.
